correctness.rationale: The source eigenvalue formula is reconstructed by an orthogonal eigenbasis and independently checked against direct symmetric Laplacians. The rare event is exactly a terminal all-one block, so Beta conjugacy yields its probability and posterior. A density limit gives n(1-P) tending to Gamma(b, rate θ); uniform conditional Laplace functionals on tight posterior sets give the Cox process. Eigenvalue errors are bounded by the tight defect count/n. Exact conditional factorial-ratio tails and an independent no-defect calculation yield the continuous Pareto-type density and complete-graph atom. All stated quantifiers require a,b>0 and k_n/n→θ∈(0,1). The included checker verifies 11507 finite exact or numerical assertions, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The problem is motivated by algebraic connectivity identified as an open quantitative direction in the source. The exact macroscopic-gap conditioning selects a polynomially rare family of graph states. Its complete order-one number of spectral defect modes has a universal Gamma–Cox law and negative-binomial count, with a sharp conditional Pareto-type gap distribution and nonzero complete-graph atom. This joint rare-event structural classification is not an arbitrary slice, and fixed-p empirical spectral theorems discard precisely the finite outlier information recovered here.
